title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a short definitional note fixing the Tate twist on (integral) mixed Hodge structures. It is the opening of the cote-18 notes on motives and Hodge theory.

The setup is a mixed Hodge structure E = (E, E_0, W_*, F^*). Here:
- E_0 is a lattice, a Z-module; Grothendieck crossed out 'espace vectoriel sur Q' and replaced it with 'module sur Z', so he wants integral MHS.
- E is the complexification of E_0.
- W is the increasing weight filtration (annotated 'croiss.').
- F is the decreasing Hodge filtration (annotated 'décr.').

He first defines a twist, keeping the same lattice E_0 inside E, by W_i(E(1)) = W_{i-2}(E) and F^i(E(1)) = F^{i-1}(E). Above this he added the marginal correction '= E(-1)'. In the now-standard convention, where Z(1) = 2πiZ has weight -2 and type (-1,-1), this formula is indeed E(-1), which raises weights by 2.

He then notes, in a parenthesis with garbled indices, that the twist is compatible with passing to graded pieces. The graded quotient Gr^W of the twist is the ordinary Tate twist of the corresponding graded quotient of E.

Finally he gives the general twist for integer n: W_i(E(n)) = W_{i+2n}(E) and F^i(E(n)) = F^{i+n}(E). This is exactly Deligne's convention, i.e. E(n) = E ⊗ Z(n).

The point of not inserting the factor (2πi)^n into the lattice is harmless abstractly. Multiplication by (2πi)^n is a C-linear map that preserves all filtrations, so it is an isomorphism of MHS between (E_0 with shifted filtrations) and E_0 ⊗ (2πi)^n Z. The factor only matters once a de Rham/Betti comparison is fixed.

The purpose is bookkeeping before the next page, which discusses transcendence degrees tied to filtrations and bigradings, comparing Betti, de Rham and Hodge. In other words, the twist is set up for the period/motivic discussion.
errors: Sign inconsistency between the two displayed definitions. The first, W_i(E(1)) = W_{i-2}(E) and F^i(E(1)) = F^{i-1}(E), is the case n = -1 of the general formula, not n = 1. Grothendieck himself flagged this with the marginal '= E(-1)'. The general formula W_{i+2n}, F^{i+n} is the standard (Deligne) one.

The graded-quotient formula is written with mismatched indices ('W_i E(-1)/W_{i-1}(E(1))'). The correct statement is Gr^W_i(E(n)) ≅ Gr^W_{i+2n}(E)(n), or with his first convention Gr^W_i(E(-1)) ≅ Gr^W_{i-2}(E)(-1).

The lattice is left unchanged, with no (2πi)^n factor. This is fine up to canonical isomorphism for abstract MHS, but not compatible with comparison isomorphisms without the factor. This is not an error per se, just a convention gap.

ideas.what: Tate twist of a mixed Hodge structure, shifting W by 2n and F by n
ideas.modern_name: Tate twist E(n) = E ⊗ Z(n) of (integral) mixed Hodge structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II (1971); twist conventions also go back to Tate and Grothendieck's motivic/ℓ-adic twists
ideas.where_published: Tate twists of ℓ-adic sheaves appear in SGA 4/5 and SGA 7. The MHS version is in Deligne's Hodge II, not in Grothendieck's own texts as far as I know.

ideas.what: Compatibility of the twist with Gr^W (graded pieces are twisted pure Hodge structures)
Insistence on an integral lattice (Z-module rather than Q-vector space)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine definitional page reproducing the standard Tate twist on MHS, with a self-corrected sign slip. It is of mild historical interest only as evidence that Grothendieck was working with Deligne's integral MHS formalism around 1969–72, as a prelude to period/transcendence questions on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'Twist de Tate sur structures de Hodge mixtes' is correct.
The annotations under W and F read 'croiss.' (croissante) and 'décr.' (décroissante). The '= E(-1)' is a marginal correction placed above 'E(1)', next to a struck-out mark.
'(twist de Tate( )' should be 'Tate(1)' or 'Tate( )'. 'effectif' is a marginal insertion under 'On définit', plausibly 'effectivement'.
The first display reads W_i(E(1)) = W_{i-2}(E), with the subscript 'i-2' written over something; the '=' in the machine reading 'W_{i=2}' is a minus sign.
Graded formula as written: 'W_i(E(-1))/W_{i-1}(E(1)) ≃ [W_i(E)/W_{i-1}(E)](-1)'. The indices are as in the manuscript and are inconsistent.
'(twist de Tate sur structures de Hodge ordinaires)' is preceded by '(on trouve donc que'.
'pour n entier n un twist' should read 'Bien sûr, on définit pour n entier un twist E(n)'.
